claims.claim: Reviewers report that the soundtrack is breathtaking and matches the emotional and action-packed moments of the game.

citations.review_text: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is one of the best games I've played. The soundtrack is absolutely breathtaking, perfectly matching every emotional and action-packed moment. Combined with its smooth, responsive gameplay and satisfying exploration, it creates an unforgettable experience. Every movement feels fluid, every area is beautifully crafted, and the music elevates the entire journey. It's a masterpiece that proves great gameplay and incredible audio can come together to create something truly special.

I was 16 when I first played this game, this is back when I had an Xbox One X. I was bored out of my mind, and could not find anything good to play, I was burned out on most of my games that I played back then anyways. I saw Ori and the Will of The Wisps on Gamepass and thought, "This looks like a little kids game, but I guess I'll give it a try." That thought was ironically the best decision I made during the 16th year of my life. 5 years later, I have bought this game on every platform I have that has this game available. Right now, I'm trying to earn every achievement (Not easy). I really appreciate the fact that this game is a "painted" game, it just adds more to the game for me, it's very unique. The water visuals, the music, the story, the flow of the animation is flawless. Gareth Cocker did an amazing job with the soundtrack for this game. 

If anybody sees this game, wondering if they should give it a try, GIVE it a try, you will NOT regret it.
  I'm hoping to this day, we'll get a continuation of the storyline

claims.claim: Reviewers note that visual effects and particles create continuous visual noise that can obscure threats and make it difficult to see what is happening during gameplay.

citations.review_text:
i enjoyed this game despite it having deal breaker game mechanics. i generally avoid games that have way too much freedom of movement, and this game is probably the worst abuser of this new age gameplay. triple jumps, hooks, glides, dashes, bashes, floating onupdrafts ect ect. heck you can even slow your falls by merely attacking in mid air, and even worse is when you grab a hook or several other hook like things, it resets all your  movements so you can repeat them over to stay floating in the air... and the game requires this madness in many sections. the final boss is full on flappy bird because they take the floor away and you have no choice to finger gymnastics to stay afloat while fighting it. its so crazy that i would rather give this game a more fitting category name like flappy bird pinball like. its not a metroidvania sorry.
there are reasons why i still enjoyed it enough to recommend it though. main one is thank goodness they kept the combat to a simple action arcade style, rather than what all these new age games are doing with precision timing and pattern recognition with memorized input coreography. the decision the devs took to not do that is what saved this game imo. the other positives about this game are the art direction which is incredibly engaging and the storyline is highly immersive. its also fairly long. took me around 20hrs (offline mode.. dont know why steam doesnt count offline hours). another huge plus is you can select the difficulty. i managed to complete it on normal mode, and only really struggled with the spider boss. i finally got him and went on to complete the game, but just the fact that theres an easy mode option, i know i can atleast restart the game in easy if i had to rage quit. many games dont have that option. theres nothing worse than buying a game that you get stuck early on and have to quit because its too hard, then you feel like you been scammed out of your money... not here.
overall i really enjoyed it despite not rea…

Bad, unsatisfying, grievous platforming. 

They don't seem to have even studied Mario at basic ass game dev camp. 

You are supposed to buffer any jump inputs received immediately before landing on a platform so that continuous jumping is possible without some inputs feeling ignored or dropped. 

Imagine the input buffering problem whilst trying to do continuous wall jumps, where the input failure condition is 'you probably fall quite far back down again'.

It's baffling to me how serious game devs can overlook such a basic aspect of platforming and still be successful. 

We truly are living in the age of visual impressiveness trumping actual gameplay because this game is a visual money shot. So many effects and particles! wow. It makes it quite hard to see wth is going on sometimes, and you will probably die to threats being obfuscated by continual visual 'noise' in combat but hey, at least it's pretty for promos. smh.

claims.claim: Reviewers report visual bugs including pixelation of background objects in later-game areas.

citations.review_text:
100% complete game.
If Blind Forest was a good game, this one is basically a masterpiece. 

Visuals and OST are amazing again (however i need to deduct some points here for the blatant pixelization bug that happens often and the only solution i found was to 200% the graphics, meaning my GPU was contantly at 85ºC, instead of 70ºC... so i rather save my GPU, lowered the graphics again and had to see those immersion breaking pixelizations). 

Gameplay is 1000% better due to having actual bosses and way more combat options. Enemies feel worth to fight in the overworld and it is satisfying. Once you have all the movement abilities, the movement is so fast, smooth and fun.

There are also quests to complete and besides 2 things (a chained delivery one and a musical combination that i had to get google's help with) they were good.

This game is definitely a HUGE recommendation (still would recommend playing Blind Forest first due to story being a direct continuation) and i can say it just slotted itself in one of my top rated games ever.

This game is amazing! I loved the story as well as the cutscenes, it felt like I was watching a movie. The graphics were also another great thing about this game, the visuals were breathtaking and really made each area shine and be more defined. I also loved at beginning of the game you unlock a few of those useful movement options early on as opposed to other games. The game's health system is very lenient as you could get away with damage tanking most obstacles. The energy system was fairly balanced though. The moves that do take energy are balanced enough to feel like you aren't losing too much at a time and there are enough energy crystals scattered around the map to regenerate that energy.

I feel like some areas of the map weren't fully tested as you could get some collectibles without the use of their intended ability but that might be me. In addition to that, the other moves that Ori uses could get a bit more usage in some spots? I like that each new move had their specific area to try it out but outside of that, I felt like I stuck to one moveset the entire playthrough. Although, I like that you could instantly switch between moves in the middle of the game as its pretty convenient so maybe that solves that problem. [b]These won't affect your gameplay that much[/b] but these are just my issues. One complaint I do have that might affect some people a little would be [spoiler]near the later-game areas the background objects would just pixelate[/spoiler]. Might just be a hardware and settings thing tho I set graphics to high.

As for game time... I haven't finished the full game yet (at the time of this review). But there are a few challenging achievements (aside from the main powerups and exploration ones) if you want to go for those. The main story on a first playthrough (if you don't skip dialogue) would be like 8-10 hrs at least.

All in all, the game is really wonderful and it shines in its graphics, story, and gameplay and I would definitely recommend th…

claims.claim: Reviewers experience confusion and dead ends in progression, requiring online guides or external searches to figure out where to go next.

citations.review_text:
Overall pretty fun. Very beautiful (especially if you're wanting to test an HDR or OLED monitor). The story was simple but wonderful, I cried. 

The music is FANTASTIC. It does a wonderful job enhancing the emotional impact at various parts of the story, and there are a few bangers among the background music for parts of the world as well. 

There are times after the "tutorial" phase of the game were it was very frustrating, and I needed to do a lot of Googling/Redditing to figure out where I was supposed to go or to find out that I need some ability from a different part of the world to continue somewhere.

Quite fun at first, interesting gameplay mechanics, and good balance. Then it gets a bit annoying, as you backtrack a lot after a couple of hours. And finally it just gets frustrating.

Don't get me wrong, the graphics are awesome for this sort of game, and the gameplay mechanics are smooth. It's just a shame that the level design and guidance are clunky, as that ruins the fun. I end up having to research things online or bang my head against a wall for a while until something makes sense. And it wasn't just one time, but multiple times. They really needed to QA the progression more before releasing this, and now that it has been out quite a while, they haven't bothered smoothing out the rough edges.

I'm sure you'll have some hardcore fans of this game who would disagree with me. But if you only have a casual interest in playing Ori, know that you'll lose interest like I did when progression gets clunky.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features hand-painted visuals, detailed sound design, and musical scores that enhance the atmosphere.

citations.review_text:
Moon Studios nailed the sequel. The controls are razor sharp; every jump, dash, and bash lands exactly when you want it to, no input lag, no fighting the game. When a platformer feels this tight, everything else just clicks into place.

Gareth Coker's soundtrack is doing serious heavy lifting too, matching the mood of Niwen beat for beat. Throw in gorgeous hand-painted visuals that still hold up years later, plus insanely detailed sound design (play with a headset as you'll hear every footstep change across every surface), and you've got a game that nails every technical box.

Story? Not spoiling it. Just go play it.

Highly recommended, especially if you're into Metroidvanias or tight platforming. One of the best games ever, easy.

Overall pretty fun. Very beautiful (especially if you're wanting to test an HDR or OLED monitor). The story was simple but wonderful, I cried. 

The music is FANTASTIC. It does a wonderful job enhancing the emotional impact at various parts of the story, and there are a few bangers among the background music for parts of the world as well. 

There are times after the "tutorial" phase of the game were it was very frustrating, and I needed to do a lot of Googling/Redditing to figure out where I was supposed to go or to find out that I need some ability from a different part of the world to continue somewhere.

Ori and the Will of the Wisps is everything a sequel and video game can be; it's pure perfection on almost every level, and, even though I tend to like sequels significantly less, it's my favorite game of all time.


[h2] Every step is a painting[/h2]

One of the core defining things about Ori is the art style; it's one of the best-looking 2D games I've ever laid my eyes on, and its sequel perfects it.
They really struck gold and kept polishing it to the maximum; every single area, every single sub-area is worth a screenshot. It's a painting that almost never ends with so much love and care put into it, and what makes it even prettier than its predecessor is how much better the effects and lighting look. Flowing water is so beautiful I almost wanna drink it with all the undiscovered bacteria inside it. Weather effects and the different times of day create such drastically different moods. The music too is wonderful, almost magical, and this all creates an atmosphere like no other.
Combine this all, and they still understand it's a game; you will always have enough clarity to understand what is part of the gameplay layer and what are background and foreground elements.


[h2] Movement like no other[/h2]

Luckily, this game doesn't just look superb; it plays great too.
Platforming and the abilities are easily my favorite. Ori's movement is so fluid, so clean, it's a genuine joy to move around, do platforming challenges, or speedrun to the next area, especially because every area has some ability and design choice that changes the way you move, but never for the worse.

This is where the abilities come into play. Ori doesn't waste your time; you get all your major abilities from the previous game back within the first 2 hours to immediately get things rolling. The bash makes a return once again, and it's as good as in the first game; it's one of Ori's defining abilities, but that's not all. claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a melee combat system with multiple weapon types and a spirit shard system for upgrades, replacing the system from the first game.

citations.review_text:
[h2]Nota Geral | Overall Rating[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]Ori and the Will of the Wisps é a evolução perfeita do que Blind Forest já tinha começado, pegando cada elemento do primeiro jogo e expandindo com mais confiança e ambição. A Moon Studios criou um metroidvania que equilibra plataforma precisa, combate muito mais robusto e uma história emocional que consegue tocar profundamente sem depender de diálogo excessivo. É raro encontrar uma sequência que supera o original em praticamente todos os aspectos, mas Will of the Wisps consegue isso com folga.[/b]

[i]Ori and the Will of the Wisps is the perfect evolution of what Blind Forest had already started, taking every element from the first game and expanding it with more confidence and ambition. Moon Studios created a metroidvania that balances precise platforming, much more robust combat, and an emotional story that manages to touch deeply without relying on excessive dialogue. It's rare to find a sequel that surpasses the original in practically every aspect, but Will of the Wisps pulls that off with room to spare.[/i]

[h2]Jogabilidade | Gameplay[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]A jogabilidade dá um salto enorme em relação ao primeiro jogo, principalmente no combate, que agora tem armas variadas como espada, arco e martelo, cada uma com seu próprio ritmo e uso tático. As novas habilidades de movimento, como o Bash aprimorado e o novo dash aéreo, criam sequências de plataforma que exigem precisão cirúrgica, mas que são extremamente satisfatórias quando você domina o timing. As lutas contra chefes também evoluíram muito, com padrões de ataque que testam de verdade tudo que você aprendeu ao longo da jornada.[/b]

[i]The gameplay takes a huge leap forward compared to the first game, especially in combat, which now features varied weapons like a sword, bow, and hammer, each with its own rhythm and tactical use. The new movement abilities, like the improved Bash and the new air dash, create platforming sequences that demand surgical pre…

As someone who followed Ori's journey from Blind Forest all the way to Will of the Wisps, I can confidently say this game is an absolute masterpiece. Moon Studios took everything that made the first game special and somehow made it even better without losing its identity.

Gameplay

The combat feels so much better this time around. There are way more abilities and Spirit Shards to experiment with, which makes every fight feel more fun. Exploration is also a huge step up. The world is bigger, movement is incredibly smooth, and simply traversing the map never gets old.

Escape Sequences

I'm so glad they kept the escape sequences. They've always been one of Ori's signature moments, and they absolutely delivered here. Every chase is intense, the music kicks in at the perfect time, and your heart just starts racing. It's still one of the coolest things this series does.

Story & Ending

...Yeah. Prepare yourself.

I genuinely didn't expect the ending to hit me this hard. The last 15 minutes completely destroyed me.

Shriek's story was absolutely heartbreaking. No redemption, just a lonely and tragic end
Saying goodbye to Naru, Gumo, and everyone Ori loved was painful enough...

Then the final reveal that the narrator was actually Ori after becoming the new Spirit Tree? That completely broke me. I just sat there watching the credits in silence!

Watching Ori grow from a tiny spirit in Blind Forest into the guardian of an entire forest in Will of the Wisps has been one of the most memorable journeys I've ever experienced in gaming.

10/10.

If you're even remotely interested in Metroidvanias, do yourself a favor and play this game.
Highly Recommended!

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that the soundtrack, composed by Gareth Coker, is an exceptional highlight of the game's presentation.

citations.review_text:
Gareth Coker is the biggest blessing on gaming soundtracks the world has ever been given.

Will of the Wisps is easily the best sequel to a game I've played, which is an incredible accomplishment given how great the first game is. They kept all the best elements of Blind Forest, managed to make them better, then took the worst elements and flipped them into something incredible too.

The rework to combat is such a welcome change, as it is no longer mindless mashing of the X button but instead a varied arsenal of both melee and ranged abilities, all to cater to your own style of play.

Boss fights are incredible set pieces within the game, blending the beloved chase sequences from the first game with more traditional combat of the metroidvania genre, making them incredibly memorable and fun to experience.

Of course, the more exceptional part of this game is the soundtrack - hitting all the right feels and only elevating how memorable the game is. This game is an absolutely incredible sequel that I highly recommend to any fan of the metroidvania genre.
Gareth Coker does his soundtrack magic again in some of the most beautiful environments ever, I will never not cry at the Ori games.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the normal difficulty setting as relatively easy, while noting that certain boss fights and optional challenge sections present notable difficulty spikes.

citations.review_text: best metroidvania game imo the gameplay is fun, graphics are incredible, and somehow the soundtrack surpasses those too. However, highly recommend doing a hard mode replay after your first playthrough, because in my opinion i found the normal mode of the game pretty easy.

PROS
- Outstanding movement and platforming.
- Greatly improved combat compared to the first game.
- Beautiful hand-crafted world with rewarding exploration.
- Gorgeous visuals and one of the best soundtracks in gaming.
- Emotional and unforgettable story.

CONS
- Difficulty spikes in a few optional challenge sections.
- Players unfamiliar with metroidvanias may occasionally get lost.

VERDICT
Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a masterpiece. Nearly every aspect, from its fluid gameplay and breathtaking visuals to its heartfelt story and incredible soundtrack is executed with exceptional quality. If you enjoy metroidvanias or simply appreciate beautifully crafted games, this is an experience you shouldn't miss.

5/5

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the map layout can be confusing to read because it lacks straight lines compared to other games in the genre.

citations.review_text:
I actually completed my first blind playthrough (which means I had absolutely no clue what this game was) on Hard + Lightless + Shardless. It took me 139 deaths and 10 hours. And let me tell you: at some point I had a mental breakdown because the damage you can do in this game was clearly meant to scale with the number of collectibles and the amount of light you get. I was getting my ass kicked during the boss fights. In comparison with the first game, where you can outskill the terrain and don't have to fight any "bosses", this setup is outright masochistic. If you are like me who thinks: "Yeah, I'm a superior gamer who rolled through the first chapter on similar difficulty, surely this one won't be any different" - YOU ARE WRONG. You will ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lose your mind.

Aside from that, the music and art are 10/10. The terrain is irritating; you easily get lost. Shards are interesting. The weapons are slightly unbalanced, but it's a single player game so it doesn't really matter. Quests are excellent. jajaja

Great game.

Certainly a step up from the Blind Forest. Like the Blind Forest, the visuals, music and map are really unique and awesome compared to other metroidvanias I have seen and played. I think that the map not having straight lines like most other metroidvanias can be a bit confusing to read at times, but it is still really cool. I am really glad now that the combat is made way more engaging instead of the auto-aim combat used in the Blind Forest.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the boss fights as having hitboxes that are difficult to reach, making certain encounters annoying to pursue.

citations.review_text: Game không hay như phần 1 dù thêm rất nhiều cơ chế vào. Điểm đầu tiên là khi t đi cái map sa mạc (map cuối cùng vẫn phải đi) tôi không biết điều đó và sau khi cực khổ lên tới đỉnh ú là chẳng gì phải lặn lội đi map khác. T còn tìm được bug đến căn phòng boss cuối nữa cơ tưởng đầu mở. Đồ họa là điểm cộng nhưng thực chất khi đánh boss nó sẽ là điểm trừ khá lớn vì ko phân biệt được hitbox hay đòn đánh của boss

Outside of the boss fights, I can agree this series remains beautiful. Very few issues were dropping the perfect 9 to an honest 8 and a half score. Mainly the beauty of the game and lore kept it within an 8 but the horrendous boss fights have to drop it a bit. I will admit this was better than Blind Forest and had slight improvements from it. 

Improvements could be saturation/brightness (it was hard to see Ori at times) and boss fights.

My biggest gripe is fighting bosses who hit boxes are hard to reach which should be an immediate thing games of this genre should avoid. It doesn't make the game hard/difficult, it makes it annoying and sad to even pursue completing the game.

I recommend because its still a great game and I enjoyed most of it.
